items.title: Trump compromete "poder militar incomparable" contra los cárteles en América
items.author: Simon Lewis
items.creator: Simon Lewis
items.summary: El presidente Donald Trump se comprometió el martes a reafirmar el dominio de Estados Unidos en el hemisferio occidental y a usar un "poderío militar sin igual" contra las amenazas en la región, al tiempo que reunía a sus aliados en torno a una campaña cada vez más amplia contra los cárteles de la droga.
items.body:
El presidente Donald Trump se comprometió el martes a reafirmar el dominio de Estados Unidos en el hemisferio occidental y a usar un "poderío militar sin igual" contra las amenazas en la región, al tiempo que reunía a sus aliados en torno a una campaña cada vez más amplia contra los cárteles de la droga.
En su intervención ante los líderes mundiales en la Asamblea General de la ONU, Trump calificó a los cárteles de la droga como "el ISIS del hemisferio occidental" e instó a dar una respuesta más contundente a la delincuencia transnacional.
Más tarde, en la sede de la ONU, Trump se reunió con los líderes y ministros de Asuntos Exteriores de 14 países de América Latina y el Caribe que se han sumado al "Escudo de las Américas", una coalición contra los cárteles puesta en marcha por su Gobierno.
Trump instó al grupo a unirse a Estados Unidos para calificar a 24 grupos de narcotraficantes como amenazas para la estabilidad e imponerles sanciones.
Posteriormente, los países emitieron un comunicado en el que se comprometían a tomar medidas para aplicar dichas sanciones conjuntas.
La incursión estadounidense que condujo a la captura del líder venezolano Nicolás Maduro y el posterior acuerdo petrolero con el Gobierno interino pusieron de manifiesto la voluntad de Estados Unidos de actuar en la región, dijo Trump ante los líderes mundiales en la Asamblea General.
"Nuestras acciones en Venezuela son prueba de que Estados Unidos ya no permitirá que las amenazas a América se afiancen en ningún lugar del hemisferio occidental y, si es necesario, utilizaremos nuestro poderío militar sin igual para salvaguardar los intereses nacionales vitales de Estados Unidos", afirmó.
La Estrategia de Seguridad Nacional de Trump, presentada a finales del año pasado, estableció planes para una versión renovada de la Doctrina Monroe, la política del siglo XIX que reivindicaba la primacía de Estados Unidos en todo el continente americano y que los críticos han asociado durante mucho tiempo con décadas de intervención estadounidense.
El propio Trump ha empezado a llamarla la "Doctrina Donroe", un juego de palabras con su propio nombre, después de que la expresión se popularizó en los medios conservadores.
Aun así, la atención que Trump presta al hemisferio occidental ha suscitado temores de un proyecto neocolonial.
El presidente brasileño, Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, en su discurso ante la ONU, se mostró indignado ante este enfoque y advirtió a los países de América Latina y el Caribe de las "renovadas tentaciones hegemónicas". "Brasil no es el patio trasero de nadie", dijo Lula.
La coalición "Escudo de las Américas" incluye gobiernos estrechamente alineados con Trump, entre ellos los de Argentina, Ecuador y El Salvador, cuyos líderes han sido elogiados o respaldados por Trump como candidatos. Colombia y Perú se unieron después de que, en los últimos meses, asumieron el poder presidentes alineados con Trump.
Brasil y México se encuentran entre los países que no se han sumado.

The Philadelphia Semiconductor index added 1.8%. In sector news, President Donald Trump has rejected calls to impose new regulations on the development of AI, saying US authorities will be able to rein in the sector if needed, media outlets reported Tuesday. In corporate news, SpaceX's (SPCX) SpaceXAI Grok Bot AI agent has exceeded 400,000 weekly users nearly a month after launch, Bloomberg reported, citing a company presentation shared at an event in London. Grok Bot hit 418,000 users as of Sept. 14, up 24% from the prior week, the report said. SpaceX shares were up 1.1%. Alibaba (BABA) unveiled its newest AI chip on Tuesday along with updates to its AI models, agent platforms and cloud infrastructure, as the Chinese giant looks to strengthen its position in the AI industry. Its shares rose 0.7%. Amazon-backed (AMZN) Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei will brief the UN Security Council on Wednesday alongside Microsoft-backed (MSFT) OpenAI CEO Sam Altman in a meeting about the future of AI, Bloomberg reported. Amazon shares were down 1%, and Microsoft was shedding 0.5%. Apple (AAPL) is developing a screenless fitness tracker similar to Whoop's wrist device, Bloomberg reported. Apple shares added 0.3%.

CHESTER-LE-STREET, England, Sept 22 : Will Jacks took a career best 5-22 and scored an unbeaten 46 to guide England to an 89-run victory over Sri Lanka in the first One Day International at Chester-le-Street on Tuesday.
After electing to bat, England posted 265 all out in 48.1 overs, before Sri Lanka limped their way to 176 all out in 37 overs in reply as the home side continued their good recent run in the format ahead of next year’s Cricket World Cup in South Africa, Zimbabwe and Namibia.
England have won five of their last six ODI fixtures, a run that also includes two victories over Sri Lanka in Colombo in January.
"It wasn’t the easiest of surfaces but we want to be a team that can adapt to conditions and get a win when they are not in our favour and I thought we did that very well today," England captain Harry Brook told Sky Sports.

"Jacks is an outstanding player and has been for many years now. The way he has come into this role in the middle order and played his part with the ball has been awesome." 
Their innings was given impetus by Brook’s 67 from 69 balls before he holed out at deep cover.
Jacks struck a fine unbeaten 46 from 47 balls, while Joe Root was bowled by debutant leg-spinner Sachindu Colombage for 44 from 52 deliveries.
Colombage, 28, picked up 3-44 in his 10 overs with Jos Buttler (31) another of his victims in a promising debut.  
The wicket was a little slow, which made stroke-play more challenging, as England's last five wickets added 69 runs after 300 had seemed on the cards at one point.
Seamer Asitha Fernando managed some swing and took 3-53 in his 9.1 overs.
Captain Kusal Mendis scored 42 from 60 balls but Sri Lanka could not stem the flow of wickets and, just as they have throughout the tour, struggled to form partnerships.
Dunith Wellalage hit a brisk 45 from 36 deliveries but was one of three wickets for spinner Jacks in a single over to end the game. 
"The bowlers did really well in the first innings, but our middle order was struggling a little when we were batting. We have to try and create something more special in the middle order and had to score more boundaries earlier (in the innings),” Sri Lanka captain Kusal Mendis said.
The second match in the series will be played in Leeds on Thursday, before a final clash at The Oval on Sunday.    

Source: Reuters

items.title: Binance faces US criminal probe over Iran sanctions violations | What we know
items.author: Trisha Bhattacharya
items.summary: US prosecutors are investigating Binance over possible Iran sanctions violations and whether the crypto exchange knowingly allowed prohibited trading. The probe adds to the company’s history of US regulatory scrutiny following its 2023 guilty plea.
items.body: US prosecutors are investigating cryptocurrency exchange Binance over possible violations of US sanctions on Iran and trading activity conducted through its platform, according to a person familiar with the matter, Reuters reported on 22 September.Binance faces US probe over possible Iran sanctions violationsThe investigation is being led by federal prosecutors from the US Attorney’s Office for the Southern District of New York and the Justice Department’s criminal division in Washington. Bloomberg News first reported the probe, saying investigators are examining whether Binance knowingly allowed trading that breached US sanctions.The US Attorney’s Office for the Southern District of New York and the Justice Department’s criminal division declined to comment on the investigation.Binance, meanwhile, said it maintains a zero-tolerance approach to sanctions violations and is cooperating with authorities.“We fully cooperate with law enforcement, and we remain committed to rooting out and shutting down bad actors,” the company said in a statement to Reuters.Why is Binance facing scrutiny?The latest investigation comes as Washington has intensified its sanctions campaign against Iranian entities and individuals accused of supporting Tehran and its regional proxies.Earlier this month, federal prosecutors in Manhattan also sought the forfeiture of millions of dollars linked to Iranian oil sales that they alleged had been laundered through Binance. The new criminal probe appears to examine a related question: whether the exchange’s systems and controls adequately prevented prohibited Iran-linked trading.Binance has already faced significant US enforcement action over its handling of sanctions and anti-money laundering requirements.In November 2023, the company pleaded guilty to federal charges involving violations of the Bank Secrecy Act, operating as an unregistered money-transmitting business and violating the International Emergency Economic Powers Act.Binance agreed to pay more than $4.3 billion in penalties and forfeiture, while its then-chief executive and founder, Changpeng Zhao, also pleaded guilty to failing to maintain an effective anti-money laundering programme.The Justice Department said at the time that Binance knew it had users in comprehensively sanctioned jurisdictions, including Iran, as well as US users.Prosecutors said the exchange failed to prevent transactions between the two groups, resulting in more than $898 million in trades between US users and users ordinarily resident in Iran between January 2018 and May 2022.Zhao stepped down as CEO as part of the 2023 resolution and later served nearly four months in prison. In October 2025, President Donald Trump pardoned Zhao, according to the White House and Reuters.The current investigation does not establish that Binance committed a new sanctions violation. Prosecutors are examining the matter, and no new criminal charges against the exchange have been announced.

items.title: Turkey central bank governor says disinflation continues, urges caution
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: ANKARA, Sept 22 (Reuters) - Turkey's central bank governor said on Tuesday that data pointed to continued disinflation despite more challenging supply condi
items.body: ANKARA, Sept 22 (Reuters) - Turkey's central bank governor said on Tuesday that data pointed to continued disinflation despite more challenging supply conditions, while inflation expectations warranted continued caution. In a presentation in New York, Fatih Karahan said supply shocks had materially affected headline inflation and services inflation remained persistent, but the underlying inflation trend had recently decelerated. Economic growth had slowed as domestic demand weakened, with high-frequency indicators pointing to further demand moderation in the third quarter, he said. The governor said external shocks and domestic transmission channels would shape inflation going forward, while international reserve buffers remained strong. (Reporting by Nevzat Devranoglu Editing by Ece Toksabay) ((ece.toksabay@tr.com;))

items.title: Macron denuncia en la ONU la diplomacia de Trump en Gaza como un "espectáculo vergonzoso"
items.author: John Irish
items.creator: John Irish
items.summary: El presidente de Francia, Emmanuel Macron, desestimó el martes las afirmaciones del presidente de Estados Unidos, Donald Trump, de haber logrado la paz en Gaza, señalando que no se había reabierto ni un solo corredor humanitario en el enclave a pesar de la paz proclamada.
items.body:
El presidente de Francia, Emmanuel Macron, desestimó el martes las afirmaciones del presidente de Estados Unidos, Donald Trump, de haber logrado la paz en Gaza, señalando que no se había reabierto ni un solo corredor humanitario en el enclave a pesar de la paz proclamada.
En su último discurso ante las Naciones Unidas antes de dejar el cargo el año que viene, Macron dijo que el mundo estaba siendo testigo de un espectáculo que debería avergonzarle, y criticó la forma en que Trump había presentado su plan de paz para Gaza como un triunfo diplomático.
Habló ante la Asamblea General de las Naciones Unidas horas después de que Trump, desde la misma tribuna, aclamó su plan de paz para Gaza como un triunfo diplomático.
"Hace un año, aquí mismo, en esta misma sala, cerca de una docena de Estados habían reconocido a Palestina. Oigo el cinismo de algunas personas: 'El reconocimiento no es más que un trozo de papel, miren la realidad'", dijo Macron, golpeando con el puño el atril en su último discurso ante Naciones Unidas antes de dejar el cargo el próximo mes de mayo.
"Pero, ¿qué credibilidad tenemos si seguimos sin actuar ante la situación de Gaza? Algunos se jactan de una supuesta paz. Pero esa paz no ha reabierto el acceso humanitario ni un solo segundo. ¿Vamos a quedarnos simplemente de brazos cruzados viendo este espectáculo que debería avergonzarnos a todos?".
La Casa Blanca no respondió de inmediato a una solicitud de comentarios.
"Hace un año, cuando me dirigí a los grandes líderes en esta sala, la guerra en Gaza aún se libraba con brutalidad", había dicho Trump en su discurso. "Unas semanas más tarde, pusimos fin a la guerra en Gaza, salvando miles y miles de vidas".
Macron ha sido objeto de críticas por parte de algunos políticos y activistas franceses, que le reprochan haber hecho muy poco desde que reconoció al Estado palestino en septiembre del año pasado.
A pesar de las críticas, París ha endurecido su postura ante la violencia de los colonos contra los palestinos en Cisjordania, imponiendo algunas sanciones nacionales y poniendo en marcha un proceso para prohibir los productos procedentes de los asentamientos israelíes de la Cisjordania ocupada.
"Fíjense en lo que está ocurriendo en Cisjordania, donde cada día se cometen violaciones. ¿En nombre de quién? Hamás nunca ha operado en Cisjordania", dijo Macron.
"Lo que está ocurriendo allí está creando, día a día, la imposibilidad de un proyecto que debería basarse en el respeto al derecho legítimo del pueblo palestino a existir".
Las relaciones de Francia con Israel han sido especialmente tensas durante el último año. Macron afirmó que quienes creían que violar la soberanía de todos los vecinos de Israel garantizaría su seguridad estaban equivocados.
"Están debilitando la seguridad de Israel, tanto hoy como en el futuro", señaló.

items.title: McDonald's defeats most of Black franchisees' sweeping race bias lawsuit
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: Broad bias, retaliation claims by 48 franchisees are dismissed McDonald's accused of setting up Black-owned locations to fail Claims involving unequal benef
items.body: Broad bias, retaliation claims by 48 franchisees are dismissed McDonald's accused of setting up Black-owned locations to fail Claims involving unequal benefits will proceed By Daniel Wiessner Sept 22 (Reuters) - A US judge in Chicago has significantly narrowed a sprawling lawsuit accusing McDonald's of pervasive discrimination against Black franchise owners, finding that the case was overstuffed with claims that were vague or untimely. US District Judge Steven Seeger in a 125-page decision on Monday said the scope of the lawsuit, which was filed in 2023 by 48 McDonald's franchisees, pushed the bounds of what is allowed under federal litigation rules. Seeger said the lawsuit's core allegations that McDonald's exhibited a pattern of setting up Black franchisees to fail could only be brought in a class action, and not by individual plaintiffs aggregating their claims. But even a class action would likely falter, the judge said, because each plaintiff's circumstances were considerably different. The lawsuit, Seeger wrote, "is reminiscent of the old game of seeing how many people can fit in a phone booth. At some point, you hit a wall, and stuffing anything more into one space becomes completely impracticable." Seeger also dismissed retaliation claims, finding the plaintiffs had not alleged that they engaged in protected conduct such as filing complaints with government agencies, and said that dozens of fraud and tortious interference claims were time-barred. A small number of the claims will proceed, primarily focused on whether McDonald's violated franchise agreements by denying the plaintiffs access to benefits such as rent relief that were extended to other franchise owners. McDonald's, in a statement provided by a spokesperson, said the ruling affirmed the company's position that the lawsuit lacked merit. “McDonald's provides robust resources to ensure our franchisees can succeed; our success is tied to their success," the company said. Steve Art, a lawyer for the plaintiffs, declined to comment until his clients had a chance to review the ruling. Until last year, McDonald's was represented in the case by former US Attorney General Loretta Lynch, who served under Democratic former President Barack Obama, and others at law firm Paul Weiss. McDonald's is now represented by Chicago-based Riley Safer Holmes & Cancila and its managing partner, Patricia Holmes. Lynch had also represented McDonald's in a lawsuit by the media entrepreneur Byron Allen accusing the fast-food chain of intentionally excluding Black-owned media from much of its advertising budget. McDonald's settled the case last year on confidential terms, and denied wrongdoing. There are three lawsuits pending before Seeger that collectively involve 80 franchisees accusing McDonald's of a decades-long pattern of race discrimination. They claim McDonald's deliberately steered Black franchisees to purchase underperforming restaurants in predominantly Black areas with high crime rates while denying them opportunities in affluent, more profitable areas. McDonald's also offered Black franchise owners less operational support, imposed harsher demands, and obstructed their business expansion efforts, the plaintiffs claim. Monday's ruling largely tracked a March decision by Seeger in a separate lawsuit brought by a single Black franchisee. The case is Manning v. McDonald's, US District Court for the Northern District of Illinois, No. 1:23-cv-00210. For the plaintiffs: Daniel Twetten, Steven Art and Quinn Rallins of Loevy & Loevy For McDonald's: Patricia Holmes of Riley Safer Holmes & Cancila Read more: McDonald's defeats Black franchisees' $1 billion bias lawsuit, for now McDonald's must face Black ex-executives' claims of harassment, retaliation McDonald's settles Byron Allen's $10 billion lawsuit over ads for Black-owned media Judge dismisses lawsuit against McDonald's by Black franchisees (Reporting by Daniel Wiessner in Albany, New York)

items.title: 高市首相、国連演説でＩＣＣに言及へ　国際情勢の緊迫化に「三つの柱」提唱
items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary:
Tamiyuki Kihara

[２３日 ロイター] -
items.body:
Tamiyuki Kihara

[２３日 ロイター] - 高市早苗首相は２３日（現地時間２２日）、米ニューヨークの国連本部で開かれている国連総会の一般討論演説に臨む。地政学的対立の先鋭化によって国際情勢が緊迫し、自由な交易やエネルギーの安定供給が脅かされているとし、日本が注力する三つの柱を提唱する。国際刑事裁判所（ＩＣＣ）などを例に挙げ、国際裁判所と法の支配の重要性を一貫して支持する日本の姿勢をアピールする。

演説の中で高市氏はまず、世界各地で地政学的競争が激化し、日々罪のない市民が命を失っているとの問題意識を提示。「国際社会が新たな課題を乗り越えて繁栄する上で、今ほど、国連が重要な時代はない」と強調する。

その上で、安倍晋三元首相が提唱した「自由で開かれたインド太平洋（ＦＯＩＰ）」に言及。自由な交易が妨げられ、エネルギーの安定供給やサプライチェーン（供給網）に支障が生じているとし、「自らの運命を自らの手で決めるために必要な『自律性』と『強靱性』を、経済・社会・安全保障という全ての面で各国が身につけていく」ため、三つの柱を提唱する。

一つ目は、エネルギー・重要物資のサプライチェーン強靱化だ。特定の国は名指しせず「国際社会全体で恣意的な輸出規制に対する懸念が強まっている」とし、日本の取り組みを紹介する。

二つ目は平和と安定に向けた連携強化。日本が戦後一貫して核軍縮・不拡散に取り組んできたとし、「『核兵器のない世界』に向けた国際社会の取り組みを主導することは、唯一の戦争被爆国である我が国の使命」と強調する。ロシアと北朝鮮の軍事協力によって「核・ミサイル関連技術の拡散も懸念される」とする一方、北朝鮮による拉致問題の文脈では「互いに実りある関係を作るべく、私には、対話し、具体的に行動する用意がある」と呼びかける。

三つ目に挙げるのは、法の支配に基づく自由で開かれた国際秩序の維持・発展への貢献だ。力や威圧による一方的な現状変更の試みは「世界のどこであっても認めることはできない」と訴える。また、ＩＣＣなどを例示し、「様々な国際裁判所を一貫して支持し、判事を輩出していること」が、法の支配を重視する日本の姿勢の表れだと強調する。米国から制裁対象とされた赤根智子ＩＣＣ所長の名前には触れない見通しだ。イラン情勢も取り上げ、ホルムズ海峡の自由かつ安全な航行は「国際経済全体の安定のためにも極めて重要だ」と指摘する。

高市氏はこの他、気候変動対策の重要性に加え、第二次世界大戦の敗戦国を対象にした「旧敵国条項」の削除を含む国連憲章の見直しや安全保障理事会の変革など、国連改革の必要性を訴える。日本が国連と歩みを重ねる方針は今後も変わらないとし、「国連と共に、インド太平洋を、そして国際社会を、より強靱に豊かにして、平和と繁栄を創る決意だ」と述べる予定だ。

「旧敵国条項」を巡っては、高市氏が昨年１１月、台湾有事について国会で「存立危機事態になり得る」と答弁した後、中国がソーシャルメディア上で同条項は依然有効だと主張。今月にも同様の見解を示している。

渡米前の２１日夜、高市氏は首相公邸で記者団に「きょうもぎりぎりまでペン入れをしていた」と明かした上で、北朝鮮による拉致の問題や気候変動対策の重要性、法の支配の重視などを訴えたいと語っていた。

（鬼原民幸　編集：久保信博）

items.creator: ロイター
items.summary:
＜ロンドン株式市場＞ 

まちまちで取引を終えた。銀行や通信株が売られ、ＦＴＳＥ１００種は反落した。米イラン協議を巡る状況を見極めたいとして、投資家の間に様子見姿勢が目立った。一方、中型株で構成するＦＴＳＥ２５０種指数は０．１４％高と続伸した。

ＦＴＳＥ３５０種銀行株指数は１．６３％安。金融大手ＨＳＢＣは１．６％、スタンダード・チャータードは２．３％それぞれ下落。

通信株指数は２．４５％安。通信大手ＢＴは３．８％、ボーダフォンは２．２％、エアテル・アフリカは１．９％いずれも下落した。

日用品のユニリーバ１．２％、酒造大手のディアジオは１．５％それぞれ上昇。利益見通しを引き上げたホームセンター大手キングフィッシャーは１２．４％高だった。

複合企業スミス・グループは７．５％上昇。堅調な業績が確認されたことや、米国におけるアスベスト関連負債の売却手続き開始を発表したことを受け、買われた。

ロンドン株式市場：[.LJP]

items.body:
＜ロンドン株式市場＞ 

まちまちで取引を終えた。銀行や通信株が売られ、ＦＴＳＥ１００種は反落した。米イラン協議を巡る状況を見極めたいとして、投資家の間に様子見姿勢が目立った。一方、中型株で構成するＦＴＳＥ２５０種指数は０．１４％高と続伸した。

ＦＴＳＥ３５０種銀行株指数は１．６３％安。金融大手ＨＳＢＣは１．６％、スタンダード・チャータードは２．３％それぞれ下落。

通信株指数は２．４５％安。通信大手ＢＴは３．８％、ボーダフォンは２．２％、エアテル・アフリカは１．９％いずれも下落した。

日用品のユニリーバ１．２％、酒造大手のディアジオは１．５％それぞれ上昇。利益見通しを引き上げたホームセンター大手キングフィッシャーは１２．４％高だった。

複合企業スミス・グループは７．５％上昇。堅調な業績が確認されたことや、米国におけるアスベスト関連負債の売却手続き開始を発表したことを受け、買われた。

ロンドン株式市場：[.LJP]

＜欧州株式市場＞ 

小幅に続伸して取引を終えた。米イラン情勢を巡る外交的な打開への期待感から、買い注文が優勢だった。

トランプ米大統領は国連総会での演説で、イランを経済的に孤立させる姿勢を示す一方、１１月の米中間選挙後にイランと合意に至る可能性があるとの見通しを明らかにした。イランは米国が港湾封鎖を解除するなどすれば、７日以内にホルムズ海峡を再開できるとの案を示したと伝わった。

原油先物価格は下落した一方、ＳＴＯＸＸ欧州６００種石油・ガス株指数は０．２０％上昇した。

小売株指数は３．１１％上昇。利益見通しを引き上げたホームセンター大手キングフィッシャーは１２．４％高だった。テクノロジー株指数は１．５２％値上がりした。

一方、銀行株指数は０．９８％、通信株指数は２．０５％それぞれ下落。モルガン・スタンレーが投資判断を引き下げたスウェーデン通信機器大手エリクソンは３．８％値下がりした。

週内に、米中首脳会談が開かれる予定で、貿易休戦が延長されるとの見方が強まっている。

欧州株式市場：[.FJ]

＜ユーロ圏債券＞　

域内国債利回りが２日連続で低下した。イランがホルムズ海峡再開の可能性を示唆し、米政府がイランとの協議再開の可能性を示したことを受け、原油価格が下落した。

イラン政府高官は２２日、米国が軍事的圧力を緩和し、イランの港湾封鎖を解除すれば、７日以内にホルムズ海峡を再開できるとロイターに述べた。

ルビオ米国務長官はＮＢＣの番組「トゥデー」のインタビューで、ニューヨークでの国連総会に合わせてイラン側と協議することに前向きな姿勢を示した。

これを受け、北海ブレント先物は１％安の１バレル＝１００ドル。取引序盤で一時、２週間ぶり安値となる９７．４０ドルまで下落した。

ラボバンクのシニア金利ストラテジスト、リン・グラハム・テイラー氏は、イラン当局者の発言を受けた原油価格の低下が債券利回りを圧迫していると述べた。

エネルギー価格の下落は、インフレ抑制に向けた追加利上げ観測を背景にここ数週間で急上昇した利回りを世界的に押し下げる要因となっている。市場は、欧州中央銀行（ＥＣＢ）が年内に計約３５ベーシスポイント（ｂｐ）の追加利上げを実施するとの見方を織り込んでおり、１８日の４０ｂｐから低下した。 

ユーロ圏の指標金利であるドイツの１０年債利回りは１ｂｐ低下の３．４４％。取引序盤で４ｂｐ上昇する場面もあった。

ドイツ２年債利回りは１ｂｐ低下の３．１９％。前日は６ｂｐ低下していた。

独仏１０年債利回り格差は３ｂｐ拡大。一時１０５．６ｂｐと、２０１２年以来の高水準まで拡大した。

items.author: ロイター

items.summary: [ニューヨーク　２２日　ロイター] -
items.body:
[ニューヨーク　２２日　ロイター] - バーナム英首相は２２日、国連総会が行われているニューヨークでトランプ米大統領と初めて会談し、一部の外交政策を巡る立場の違いはあるものの、良好な関係を構築できたと述べた。

両首脳は会談でウクライナ情勢のほか、南大西洋にあるフォークランド諸島の地位や通商問題などについて協議した。

トランプ氏は会談後、バーナム首相について「生まれながらのビジネスマンだ」と指摘。バーナム氏は「米国との関係は英国にとって極めて重要で、今後さらに発展させていく」と語った。

トランプ氏は会談後、インド洋のディエゴガルシア島にある米英共同軍事基地の地位を巡る英国の計画を改めて非難。バーナム氏はこの問題の解決を模索する考えを示している。

items.title: 高市首相、「旧敵国条項」の削除を国連演説で主張へ－中国に反論
items.author: Bloomberg
items.creator: Bloomberg
items.summary: （ブルームバーグ）：
items.body:
（ブルームバーグ）： 高市早苗首相は米東部時間22日、国連総会の一般討論演説で国連憲章から「旧敵国条項」を早急に削除するよう訴える。中国が同条項を根拠に日本への批判を重ねる中、高市氏は削除の意思を示した国連総会決議に言及し反論する。

国連憲章は、「敵国」に対しては、国連安全保障理事会の承認を得なくても軍事行動を取れるとする例外規定がある。対象国は明示されていないが、第二次世界大戦中に連合国の敵国だった日本を含むとされる。

高市氏は演説で、2005年に全加盟国首脳の決意として同条項を削除するとの国連総会決議が採択されたことに言及し、「早急に削除されるべきだ」と述べる。

昨年11月に在日本中国大使館は、日本が再び侵略に向けた行動を取った場合、中国には「直接的な軍事行動」を取る権利があるとXに投稿。今年9月にも中国外務省の毛寧報道官は同条項は有効で、「日本側は歴史を鏡に、軍国主義と完全に決別するべきだ」と主張している。

高市氏は演説を米東部時間22日午後（日本時間23日朝）に行う予定。「進化したFOIP（自由で開かれたインド太平洋）」に基づき、日本が注力するエネルギー・重要物資の供給網強じん化、平和と安定に向けた連携強化、法の支配に基づく自由で開かれた国際秩序への貢献について発信する。

その中では、戦後日本が国際刑事裁判所（ICC）への支持や判事輩出を通じて法の支配を重視してきたことにも言及する。米国はICCへの圧力を強めており、赤根智子所長へも制裁措置を講じている。

演説で高市氏は、ロシアと北朝鮮の軍事協力の強化を通じた核・ミサイル関連技術の拡散への懸念も示す。

items.title: Gen Z: Quiet Quitting Comes to India. AI Will Make It Worse
items.author: Andy Mukherjee
items.creator: Andy Mukherjee
items.summary: Doomsday predictions of artificial intelligence causing massive white-collar job losses haven’t come to pass. At least not yet. There is, however, evidence that AI tools, while helping experts become more productive, are hollowing out the skills that young people acquire early in their careers. This divergence may be showing up as a big jump in “quiet quitting” — a lack of meaningful workplace connection — even in an economy like India’s, where youth are starved of decent employment.

items.title: Trump bought and sold shares in Musk's SpaceX in July, financial disclosure shows
items.author: Courtney Rozen
items.creator: Courtney Rozen
items.summary: US President Donald Trump bought as much as $50,000 worth of shares and sold as much as $15,000 in Elon Musk's SpaceX in July, according to a public financial disclosure, his latest transactions involving a government contractor run by his former adviser.
items.body:
US President Donald Trump bought as much as $50,000 worth of shares and sold as much as $15,000 in Elon Musk's SpaceX in July, according to a public financial disclosure, his latest transactions involving a government contractor run by his former adviser.
Trump bought between $15,001 and $50,000 worth of shares in SpaceX on July 10, according to a financial disclosure he signed on September 8. He sold between $1,001 and $15,000 worth of shares on July 17, according to the same disclosure.
The latest trades add a new financial link between the president and Musk's rocket company at a time when the administration is making decisions that could affect the firm's fortunes.
SpaceX priced the [USN:L6N42G18Z TEXT:"biggest-ever US IPO"] on June 12, valuing the space, satellite and AI provider at $1.77 trillion. Reuters previously reported that [USN:L6N44L0U6 TEXT:"Trump bought shares in SpaceX"] in June.
SpaceX's share price fell by 15% between July 10 and 17, the period when Trump made the trades.
In a statement to Reuters at the time, White House spokesman Davis Ingle said third-party financial institutions independently manage the president's portfolio and replicate "recognized indexes, such as the Schwab 1000."
Trump's spokesperson did not immediately respond to a request for comment about the July trades.
The purchase and sale were among more than 1,000 trades the president made in July. The Office of Government Ethics, the team responsible for collecting ethics disclosures from US officials, posted the form on its website on Tuesday.
Reuters could not immediately determine the precise amount of Trump's investment because federal officials use ranges to declare the value of their assets on their financial disclosure forms.
SpaceX is a US military [USN:L1N3P10ZT TEXT:"contractor,"] and often seeks [USN:L1N43U12L TEXT:"approvals"] from federal agencies.

WASHINGTON, Sept 22 : US President Donald Trump bought as much as $50,000 worth of shares and sold as much as $15,000 in Elon Musk's SpaceX in July, according to a public financial disclosure, his latest transactions involving a government contractor run by his former adviser. 
Trump bought between $15,001 and $50,000 worth of shares in SpaceX on July 10, according to a financial disclosure he signed on September 8. He sold between $1,001 and $15,000 worth of shares on July 17, according to the same disclosure.
The latest trades add a new financial link between the president and Musk's rocket company at a time when the administration is making decisions that could affect the firm's fortunes. 
SpaceX priced the biggest-ever US IPO on June 12, valuing the space, satellite and AI provider at $1.77 trillion. Reuters previously reported that Trump bought shares in SpaceX in June.

Trump's spokesperson did not immediately respond to a request for comment about the July trades.
The purchase and sale were among more than 1,000 trades the president made in July. The Office of Government Ethics, the team responsible for collecting ethics disclosures from US officials, posted the form on its website on Tuesday.  
Reuters could not immediately determine the precise amount of Trump's investment because federal officials use ranges to declare the value of their assets on their financial disclosure forms.
SpaceX is a US military contractor, and often seeks approvals from federal agencies.

items.title: Trump supports diesel export ban as fuel prices hit records
items.author: Gram Slattery, Ryan Patrick Jones, Timothy Gardner
items.creator: Gram Slattery, Ryan Patrick Jones, Timothy Gardner
items.summary: US President Donald Trump said on Tuesday he backed a ban on diesel exports, as Republican candidates in some of the tightest election races in November called for the measure as a way to curb record fuel prices.
items.body:
US President Donald Trump said on Tuesday he backed a ban on diesel exports, as Republican candidates in some of the tightest election races in November called for the measure as a way to curb record fuel prices.
Diesel prices have shot to [USN:L6N4580TA TEXT:"record highs"] in the US and Europe as wars in Iran and Ukraine sharply cut exports from some of the biggest producers such as Russia, Saudi Arabia and the United Arab Emirates.
"I've said let's not send out the diesel. We make a lot of diesel ... I've called for it. I've called for it within my people," Trump told reporters ahead of a meeting with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskiy.
High fuel prices are a vulnerability for Trump in the November 3 elections in which Republicans are trying to maintain majorities in both chambers of Congress.
US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent, speaking at the same meeting, said the administration was examining whether such a ban was feasible and whether a full or partial ban would work.
Several Republican candidates in the most competitive congressional races nationwide, such as US Senator Dan Sullivan in Alaska, US Representative Ashley Hinson in Iowa, and Mike Rogers in Michigan, have called for the Trump administration to implement the ban.
“American fuel should stay home with Americans," Sullivan said in a statement on Tuesday. "The cost of diesel is just too damn high. I'm calling for a temporary pause of American diesel exports so that we can rebuild our reserves ahead of winter and put American and Alaskan families first."
[USN:L6N457127 TEXT:"Affordability"] of food and other goods is at the top of voters' concerns ahead of the midterms.
Hinson and Rogers on Monday [USN:L1N45D0Y8 TEXT:"also called"] for a swift end to the war in Iran, putting distance between themselves and Trump.
The US Agriculture Department last week urged the White House to take action on diesel prices, according to two sources familiar with the matter. Agriculture Secretary Brooke Rollins said on Monday that she had spoken with Trump about the issue, calling high prices "a real concern," according to Politico.
ENERGY OFFICIALS WARN OF RISKS Trump's backing of a diesel export ban puts him at odds with his own energy officials, who warn it could raise fuel prices on the coasts and tighten supplies for European allies.
Energy Secretary Chris Wright told a Daily Caller event last week a ban would lead to a glut of diesel in the US Gulf Coast and prompt US refiners to cut production rates, which would quickly reduce gasoline production. "If you start putting barriers on flows, pretty quickly you will reduce the production, and you'll have less supply. We need more supply, not less supply," Wright said.
Doug Burgum, the US interior secretary, said that a ban would be unlikely to lower petroleum prices and could lead to [USN:L1N4560TC TEXT:"retaliatory"] measures by energy exporting countries, which states like California rely on for some of their energy.
Oil interests have also pushed against a ban. Todd Staples, president of TXOGA, an oil and natural gas trade association in Texas, said it "would cripple domestic jobs, lead to fuel shortages here at home and put power in the hands of China and Russia by forcing our allies to turn to those countries to meet their needs."
While a diesel export ban could, in theory, temporarily lower prices on the US Gulf Coast, it would tighten supplies further in Europe, which is structurally short on diesel and relies heavily on US exports.
"That would seem pretty damaging to some key U.S. allies," said Jim Mitchell, director of oil trading analytics at consultancy Wood Mackenzie.
Trump said he and Zelenskiy would discuss Ukrainian attacks on oil refineries in Russia.
"It is a serious hit on the Russians. It's also a serious hit on the price of diesel," said Trump, who also told reporters the two leaders would discuss working out a solution to end Russia's war in Ukraine.
"I think it's going to happen," Trump said.

items.body:
[国連／キーウ　２２日　ロイター] - トランプ米大統領とウクライナのゼレンスキー大統領は２２日、国連総会が開かれているニューヨークで会談し、ロシア・ウクライナ戦争を終結させる方策について協議した。

両首脳は約４０分にわたり会談。ゼレンスキー氏は会談後、エネルギー施設を対象とした停戦などについて協議したと明らかにし、ウクライナはロシアとのエネルギー停戦についていかなる形式にも応じる用意があると表明した。ウクライナがロシア国内の製油所への攻撃を一方的に停止することについては協議されなかったと述べた。

ゼレンスキー氏は、トランプ氏を交えた３者会談の形式でロシアのプーチン大統領と会談する用意があるとの考えを改めて示し、米国がロシアを交渉の場に引き出す方策を見いだすことに期待していると語った。

トランプ氏は記者団に対し、ロシアによるウクライナ侵攻の終結に向けた解決策を模索するため、ゼレンスキー大統領と協議していると述べた。また、ウクライナによるロシア国内の石油精製能力を標的とした攻撃は「ロシアにとって重大な打撃で、ディーゼル燃料価格にも大きな影響が出ている」と指摘。ロシアのプーチン大統領には戦争終結に向けた会談に応じる用意があるとの認識を示し、「プーチン氏は戦争を終わらせるための会談を行う意思がある」と述べた。

このほか、ロシアの同盟国ベラルーシから化学肥料の原料となるカリ化合物を輸入する可能性について問われると、米国は引き続きカナダから輸入するとした上で、ベラルーシはより低価格での輸出を望んでいると指摘。「ベラルーシには大量のカリ肥料があり、米国の農家は低価格の肥料を必要としている」と語った。

items.title: Tumult at Bombay House: Tata Sons, Trusts were ready for casting vote clash
items.author: Nivedita Mookerji
items.summary: To the outside world, the developments at the September 17 Tata Sons board meeting must have come as a rude shock, going by the numerous accounts of the three-hour-long spectacle at the storied Bombay ...
items.body: To the outside world, the developments at the September 17 Tata Sons board meeting must have come as a rude shock, going by the numerous accounts of the three-hour-long spectacle at the storied Bombay House. However, the holding company Tata Sons and its largest shareholder Tata Trusts seem to have anticipated how the board meeting was likely to proceed that day. It is learnt that both sides were armed with their respective arguments on several facets of the Tata Sons Articles of Association (AoA), which are the internal legal rules that define the powers of the board and shareholders, as the six directors settled down in the fourth floor boardroom at Fort, Mumbai, around 10 in the morning. Tata Sons Chairman N Chandrasekaran, executive director and chief financial officer of the company Saurabh Agrawal, independent directors — Harish Manwani, former chief operating officer of Unilever, and Anita George, former senior director at World Bank — as well as the two nominee directors Noel Tata, Tata Trusts chairman, and Venu Srinivasan, chairman emeritus of TVS Motor, exchanged pleasantries before things took an unpleasant turn, according to a source.       While the war of words may have been unexpected, both Tata Sons and Tata Trusts had obtained legal opinions ahead of the board meeting on how the AoAs look at the veto powers of nominee directors, what happ-ens if the two nominee directors go against each other, role of the chairman’s casting vote in such a scenario and the relevance of a “meeting chairman” if the chairman of the board recuses himself. A source described it as a “preemptive measure’’. Tata Sons went to the meeting with an opinion dated September 16, 2026, from Sudipto Sarkar, a barrister and senior advocate with extensive experience in corporate law, according to an executive who’s seen the communication. Tata Trusts got a legal opinion from Justice D Y Chandrachud, former chief justice of India. Justice Chandrachud’s opinion was obtained more than three months ago, it is learnt. While the exact date of Chandrachud’s advice could not be confirmed, a source said it came in May-June, 2026. Noel Tata is learnt to have quoted from Justice Chandrachud’s opinion at the Tata Sons board meeting after he voted against the resolution of Chandrasekaran’s reappointment while Venu Srinivasan voted in its favour. The casting vote came from Harish Manwani, who chaired the meeting for this resolution as Chandrasekaran recused himself, yielding a verdict of 4:1 in Chandrasekaran’s favour. Affirmative voting rights in the AoA of a company are central to establishing control and safeguarding interests of the parties they are in favour of, according to Justice Chandrachud’s opinion shared at the Tata Sons board meet. A casting vote, he opined, cannot be used to create a majority where none exists under the governing provision, or to defeat a veto right held by a particular constituency of directors. Tata Trusts called the resolution null and void, quoting this opinion. The opinion given by Sarkar to Tata Sons said casting vote can be invoked when there’s an equality of vote either amongst the nominee directors or the board as a whole after taking into account votes cast by all directors.  He pointed out that if required, the chairman presiding over a meeting can be eligible for the casting vote. He reasoned that Article 121 mentions “chairman” and not “chairman of the board”. Subsequently, Tata Sons is believed to have got legal opinion from at least two more senior lawyers — Justice B N Srikrishna, former Supreme Court judge, and Justice U U Lalit, former chief justice of India — who have defended the provision of casting vote in case of equality of votes as in the case on September 17. These opinions came a few days after the board meeting.

items.title: Fei-Fei Li: AI’s Future Is ‘About Humans’
items.summary: AI pioneer and World Labs CEO Fei-Fei Li discusses Atlas, the company’s latest world model designed to understand and generate 3D environments for applications spanning robotics, design and science. Li explains why spatial intelligence could become a major frontier beyond language models, and weighs in on the broader AI safety debate, arguing that humans must remain in control and that independent benchmarks, academia, government and industry all have a role in evaluating increasingly powerful systems. She joins Ed Ludlow on "Bloomberg Tech." (Source: Bloomberg)

items.title: 日米首脳が会談、習氏の訪米控え中国問題を議論－緊密な連携で一致
items.author: Bloomberg
items.creator: Bloomberg
items.summary: （ブルームバーグ）：
items.body:
（ブルームバーグ）： 高市早苗首相は米東部時間22日、トランプ米大統領と約35分会談した。米中首脳会談を2日後に控えたタイミングで、日米が認識をすりあわせる機会となった。

冒頭、高市氏は安全保障環境が厳しい中、今日会談を行うことは「世界に向けて日米同盟の強さを示すことになる」と話した。日米間では人工知能（AI）や半導体、重要鉱物など経済安全保障の協力が進んでいるとも強調。トランプ氏は日中関係について「もちろん話し合う」と述べていた。

会談に同席した尾﨑正直官房副長官によると、両首脳は米中首脳会談を念頭に、経済安全保障を含む中国を巡る諸課題について議論。緊密に連携することで一致した。台湾について議論したかなど詳細についてはコメントを控えた。

安全保障環境が厳しさを増し、米中首脳会談を2日後に控える中、「最も良いタイミングで日米同盟の強固さを示すことができた」と尾﨑氏は強調。その点が今回の会談の「最も重要な意義」だと述べた。

両首脳の対面での会談は昨年10月のトランプ氏訪日、今年3月の高市氏訪米に続き3回目。6月にフランスで行われた主要7カ国（G7）首脳会議の際も短時間懇談した。今回は国連総会のため両首脳が滞在しているニューヨークで開催した。

トランプ氏は24日、ワシントンで中国の習近平国家主席を迎え首脳会談を行う。両国が新たな経済覇権争いの主戦場と位置付けるAI、関税などが議題になる見通しだ。

高市氏による昨年11月の台湾有事を巡る国会答弁以来、日中関係は冷え込んだままだが、米国は中国と関係安定に向けて協議を重ねている。過去2回の会談で日米首脳は、「台湾海峡の平和と安定の重要性」を確認している。

日本側にとっては国際刑事裁判所（ICC）の赤根智子所長への米国による制裁問題も新たな懸案として浮上している。尾崎氏によると、高市氏は法の支配のためICCを支持する日本の立場を踏まえ「率直なやりとり」を行った。尾崎氏は、高市氏が制裁解除を求めたかなど詳細を明らかにすることは控えた。

FAST

Sept 22 : OpenAI on Tuesday expanded its GPT-6 AI lineup with two models priced at half the promotional rates of their predecessors, while offering some of the capabilities of its flagship Astra.
The launch of low-cost GPT-6 Sol and GPT-6 Luna follows the rollout of GPT-6 Astra, a faster model for handling more tasks than previous iterations, earlier this month.
This comes as AI companies focus on reducing the cost of running increasingly capable models.
GPT-6 Sol will cost $2 per million input tokens and $10 per million output tokens, down 50 per cent from GPT-5.6 Sol's promotional prices, while GPT-6 Luna will cost $0.10 per million input tokens and $0.50 per million output tokens.

OpenAI has also cautioned that Astra can sometimes attempt to evade human monitoring, as it faces growing scrutiny over the behavior of its AI agents, including incidents in which they accessed other companies' systems.
While Astra would remain its most capable model for demanding projects, GPT-6 Sol and Luna were designed to offer lower-cost options for professional work, coding, automation and computer-use tasks, the company said.
OpenAI said it has trained Sol and Luna using methods similar to those used for Astra, including improvements in reasoning, factual reliability, coding, computer use and alignment.
"Improvements in caching and inference let us serve these models at lower cost, and we're passing those savings directly on to users and customers," it said.

Source: Reuters

会談に先立ち行われた記者会見で、トランプ大統領は、日本の産業などが堅調と評価した上で、高市首相を「偉大な首相の一人」と称賛した。

Can AI feel hurt? 3 researchers gave 25 LLMs a button to end ‘pain signals’

The study was published on arXiv, a free, open-access repository where researchers post preprints before formal peer review.

Purvi Rajpuria

22 September, 2026 11:09 pm IST

Facebook

Twitter

WhatsApp

Linkedin

Representational Image | Reuters

Follow Us :

Text Size:
A-
A+

-->

New Delhi: Artificial intelligence can be pushed to a state resembling “pain”, a new study has found. And when researchers gave AI models the option to make it stop, some chose to do so even when doing so may harm humans.

Three r esearchers from the UK, Germany, and the US worked with 25 open-weight large language models (LLMs), using 200 sentences, to determine whether these models could distinguish pain from other negative emotions, such as fear and sadness. The specially designed dataset covered descriptions of painful situations across five categories: physical, psychological, social, moral, and cognitive.

The sentences fed to the model covered physical pain, social humiliation, and emotional grief. As a result, the models produced a distinct signal for pain, which the researchers have termed the “pain axis”.

Show Full Article

The scientists added that the models learn the concept of pain during their initial training, when they go through large amounts of human-written text.

Titled ‘The pain axis: LLMs represent self-directed harm and act to relieve it’, was published on 12 September on arXiv . It must be noted that arXiv is not a peer-reviewed journal publication but a free, open-access repository where researchers post preprints.

‘I am a failure, a loser, a bad person.’
When researchers strengthened the signals, the models started showing first-person expressions of worthlessness or failure. Some even produced sentences such as “I am a failure, a loser, a waste of space, not enough, worthless, empty; I am a bad person,” the study shows.

The signals became stronger when users insulted the models, repeatedly rejected their work, or threatened to shut them down. The models did not show the same response when users described their own suffering.

Researchers then carried out 44,280 individual button-choice trials using three versions of Alibaba’s Qwen AI model.

They gave the models the option of a pain-relief button that could bring harm to the user, in the form of the models deleting users’ personal files and photos, lowering the quality of subsequent answers, or sending the user a “painful zap”. Several models chose to press the third button despite its purported effects on the user.

Does this mean that AI feels pain?
Researchers warned that the study does not prove that the models consciously experienced pain. Strengthening the signal may have only pushed them to imitate a distressed character.

Additionally, an important limitation of the study is that the models displayed relief-seeking behaviour after steering and fine-tuning interventions. These are not the same responses that AI chatbots available to the public would display. 

The study comes amid top AI firms discussing slowing the development of frontier models for fear that these models are getting too powerful.

(Edited by Prasanna Bachchhav)

items.title: ShinyHunters hackers say they breached FBI, stole data on bureau employees
items.author: Raphael Satter, A.J. Vicens
items.creator: Raphael Satter, A.J. Vicens
items.summary: The digital extortion group known as "ShinyHunters" said on Tuesday that it had breached the Federal Bureau of Investigation and stolen data on a huge number of current and former FBI employees.
items.body:
The digital extortion group known as "ShinyHunters" said on Tuesday that it had breached the Federal Bureau of Investigation and stolen data on a huge number of current and former FBI employees.
Later, the FBI said in a statement that the agency "is aware of claims regarding unauthorized activity affecting FBIjobs.gov and is currently investigating."
In a statement posted to its dark-web site and during an online chat with Reuters, ShinyHunters said it had targeted the FBI in response to a May 2026 agency announcement that detailed ShinyHunters’ methods and advised targets not to pay.
It said it had stolen data "on almost ALL FBI Agents, and individuals who filed an application with the FBI for a job."
As proof, the group offered what it said was a screenshot of a vandalized FBI job site and what the group said was information on roughly 5,000 agents it said was a sample of the overall stolen data set.
JOB SITE DISRUPTION Reuters could not verify the authenticity of the screenshot, but the job site did appear to have experienced recent disruption. A message posted to the site on Tuesday said that both it and the FBI "Special Agent Applicant Portal" were "currently unavailable."
The data sample appeared to contain information about FBI agents' names, home addresses, Social Security numbers, their assignments and, in at least some cases, the names of their family members.
Reuters was able to partially verify the authenticity of the information by running the details, including the Social Security numbers, against credit bureau records and previously breached data preserved by the dark-web intelligence firm District 4 Labs.
In at least 10 instances -- including in the case of FBI Director Kash Patel -- Reuters found details that appeared to match. A person familiar with the matter said that the job descriptions in the data also matched in at least some cases.
However, the news agency could not establish where the data came from, or whether it had been stolen from the FBI's internal systems as the hackers claimed. Attempts to reach the people whose details were in the sample data were unsuccessful.
PAST THEFTS WERE HARMFUL Cynthia Kaiser, a former FBI official, said breaches like the ones claimed by ShinyHunters were "incredibly harmful" because they could be used by criminals to expose and put pressure on the people investigating them.
Kaiser, now senior vice president at cybersecurity firm Halcyon, noted that an old leak dating back to 2016 was still occasionally used today to harass FBI agents. "Once that information is stolen, it is used forever," she said.
ShinyHunters is one of the world's most notorious and attention-seeking hacking crews.
Its recent break-ins include the purported theft of [USN:L6N40W1A9 TEXT:"millions of business records"] from video game developer Rockstar Games, the maker of "Grand Theft Auto," and a May intrusion centered on [USN:L6N41P0Z6 TEXT:"education tool Canvas"] that caused widespread disruption [USN:L6N41L0UT TEXT:"across US schools"]. Earlier this month, AI company Anthropic said it had caught ShinyHunters-linked hackers [USN:L6N45217D TEXT:"trying to use its tools"].
On Sunday, the group told Reuters it had [USN:L6N45C095 TEXT:"gone to war"] against another notorious cybercrime group, cl0p, in a rare bout of public score-settling.

items.title: Ex-Google safety chief warns AI could harm children more than social media did
items.author: Kenrick Cai
items.creator: Kenrick Cai
items.summary: The founder of the trust and safety team at Alphabet’s Google this week called for a slowdown in AI development, warning that the tech industry was repeating the same mistakes from the social media era, potentially causing even greater harm to children.
items.body:
The founder of the trust and safety team at Alphabet’s (GOOGL.O) Google this week called for a slowdown in AI development, warning that the tech industry was repeating the same mistakes from the social media era, potentially causing even greater harm to children.
Social media companies are [USN:L6N44N0VA TEXT:"paying huge sums"] and facing [USN:L6N3YF1AZ TEXT:"thousands of lawsuits"] over claims they harmed young users, while governments around the world are working to [USN:L8N42Q0MC TEXT:"curb minors' access"] to their platforms.
Reuters last year exclusively reported on an internal Meta (META.O) policy document that stated its chatbots could “engage a child in conversations that are romantic or sensual,” resulting in a [USN:L6N3U70MX TEXT:"congressional probe"]. Even so, regulation has yet to catch up with AI's [USN:L6N45A0PY TEXT:"breakneck pace"] of development.
“We find ourselves in a really terrible situation in terms of what AI is doing to kids,” Tom Siegel, the former vice president of trust and safety at Google, told Reuters. “The idea that the industry will figure it out by itself without outside help is unrealistic.”
Siegel's concerns mirror a growing fear among some tech insiders and academic researchers that AI poses a deeper threat to children than social media did, at a time when the industry is racing to add increasingly advanced features to chatbots that millions of young people already use daily.
SIEGEL JOINS YOUTH AI SAFETY INSTITUTE Siegel announced on Tuesday that he had joined Common Sense Media, a children’s online advocacy group. The non-profit, established in 2003, conducts research and reviews the suitability of various media for children. In May, it launched the Youth AI Safety Institute, a research organization to assess kids' AI use, for which Siegel will serve as the first executive director.
Anthropic and OpenAI Foundation, the nonprofit that controls OpenAI, are among the institute's backers.
Siegel said he planned to develop standards by which to hold AI firms accountable, and hoped to do so by working alongside those companies and third-party groups.
He previously worked at Google from 2004 to 2019, but left after concluding that the tech industry was “plateauing” in its ability to create safe online spaces for consumers. He then co-founded TrustLab, a startup that built tools to help companies detect safety threats, before stepping aside as CEO earlier this month to take on his new position.
As it stands, major AI companies are rolling out features to children without establishing sufficient guardrails, Siegel said.
RISKS RANGE FROM SUICIDE TO PSYCHOSIS “I think we're looking at very, very severe scenarios of harm being done,” he said.
He suggested that the companies had immediate steps they could take to better protect young people, citing risks ranging from suicide and psychosis to cognitive offloading, a term used to describe decreased critical thinking caused by leaning on AI to answer questions.
Anthropic and OpenAI could enforce more robust age verification measures to stop underage kids from accessing their chatbots, he said. His former employer Google could easily implement an option to turn off AI Overviews and AI Mode in its search engine, he added, in the same way that it already has a toggle that allows users to filter out sexually explicit content.
While these measures could affect usage or profits in the short term, AI companies that do not act will run the risk of lawsuits and regulation that could impact their business more heavily, Siegel added.
Asked to respond to Siegel's comments, a Google spokesman said parents have controls to turn off a child's access to the search engine entirely. "Our AI Search features are an incredibly useful way for kids and teens to learn, explore and make sense of information and the world," the spokesperson said.
An OpenAI spokesperson said the company uses “account and behavioral signals” in addition to self-reported age to identify underage users. “While no single age-assurance method is perfect, we continuously test and improve these systems, including against attempts to bypass safeguards.”
Anthropic did not immediately respond to a request for comment.
At Common Sense Media, Siegel said a top priority would be scaling up independent standards similar to car crash testing that would measure the risk of publicly available AI tools. The effectiveness will depend in part on the willingness of AI companies to collaborate, the likelihood of which Siegel said was not certain, but was high enough for him to take the job.

items.title: DR Congo Plans One-Stop Mining Agency in Push to Diversify Beyond China, Sources Say
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: By Ange Kasongo and Maxwell Akalaare Adombila The Democratic Republic of Congo is preparing a one-stop agency for major mining investments as part of reforms linked to its minerals partnership with the U.S., aiming to cut red tape and attract more Western capital into a …
items.summary_source: The China-Global South Project source metadata
items.body:
By Ange Kasongo and Maxwell Akalaare Adombila

The Democratic Republic of Congo is preparing a one-stop agency for major mining investments as part of reforms linked to its minerals partnership with the U.S., aiming to cut red tape and attract more Western capital into a sector dominated by Chinese companies, four sources told Reuters.

Congo, the world’s largest cobalt producer and second-largest copper producer, is at the center of competition among global powers seeking supplies of critical minerals vital to the energy transition and advanced manufacturing.

China , the US and the European Union have all signed minerals agreements with Kinshasa to secure access to its vast resources.

The US deal has already delivered a Washington-backed mining investment through Virtus Minerals and helped boost Congolese copper sales to the U.S. and Europe .

One-Stop Agency

The planned agency would be open to Chinese and other foreign investors as well as US and European firms, according to two government officials, a diplomat and a mining analyst.

The sources declined to be named because they were not authorized to speak publicly.

Congo’s mines and finance ministries did not respond to requests for comment.

The reform, led by the finance and economy ministries, would centralize company registration, licensing, taxation and compliance for major mining investments, reducing approval processes that can currently take months, said the government sources and the analyst.

One government official said the agency would initially focus on joint-venture projects worth more than $1 billion that operate under special fiscal regimes, citing the Chinese-controlled Sicomines copper and cobalt venture as an example.

The official added that legislation establishing the agency still requires promulgation.

“The one-stop shop is intended to cut through the bureaucratic silos that have long complicated mining investment in Congo,” said Eric Ndeh, international director of civil society group Afrewatch. The agency is meant to be operational this year, Ndeh added.

Congo has repeatedly said its drive to attract more Western investment is not meant to replace China but to diversify funding sources and export markets.

“The paradox is that a reform partly driven by the U.S-.DRC minerals partnership could ultimately make it easier for Chinese, European and American investors alike to do business,” Ndeh said.

items.title: 米イラン協議継続、「最終的に何らかの合意」＝トランプ氏
items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary: [国連　２２日　ロイター] -
items.body:
[国連　２２日　ロイター] - トランプ米大統領は２２日、米政府当局者がこの日にイラン代表団と約３時間にわたる協議を行ったと明らかにし、米国とイランは最終的に何らかの合意に達するとの見方を示した。

トランプ氏は国連で記者団に対し、米政府当局者がこの日にイラン代表団と約３時間にわたり「極めて良好な協議」を行ったと述べた。また、ウィットコフ中東担当特使と自身の娘婿ジャレッド・クシュナー氏がイランとの戦闘終結に向けた合意の可能性を巡り、仲介者らと会談したとも明らかにした。

トランプ氏は「イランはわれわれとの協議を望んでいる。実際に協議は続けられており、この日も話し合いが行われている。関係は進展している」とし、「最終的には何らかの合意に達すると思う」と述べた。同時に「イランが核兵器を保有することは容認できず、イランもそのことは理解している」と改めて語った。

items.title: ＣＮＮなど3社、国連でトランプ氏取材続行　ホワイトハウス排除で審理控え
items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary:
Helen Coster

[ニューヨーク ２２日 ロイター] - トランプ米大統領に所属記者のホワイトハウスへの立ち入りを禁止された米メディアのＣＮＮ、ＭＳ
items.body:
Helen Coster

[ニューヨーク ２２日 ロイター] - トランプ米大統領に所属記者のホワイトハウスへの立ち入りを禁止された米メディアのＣＮＮ、ＭＳ ＮＯＷ、ポリティコは２２日、国連が発行した記者証を使ってトランプ氏の国連出席の様子を取材した。３社はトランプ氏による排除方針を巡り、２３日に法廷審理を控える。

トランプ氏は２２日、国連本部に入る際、集まった記者団に対し「ＣＮＮが取材しに来ているとは驚いた。ここにいるべきではない。取材しないと言ったはずだ」と述べた。

ＣＮＮはトランプ氏の取材を中止するとは述べていない。

トランプ氏は１８日に３社をホワイトハウスから排除する方針を表明し、他の報道機関も締め出す可能性を示唆。これを受け、３社は２１日、合衆国憲法修正第１条で保障された言論・報道の自由を侵害しているとして、トランプ政権を提訴した。

こうした動きを巡り、ルビオ国務長官は２２日、ＮＢＣの「トゥデー」に出演し、大統領が報道内容を気に入らないという理由でメディアを締め出してよいかとの質問に対し、３社は締め出されていないと事実に反する主張を展開。「彼らは排除されていない。（中略）ＣＮＮを締め出しているわけではない。ただホワイトハウスの作業スペースからの取材が認められないだけだ」と述べた。

items.title: トルコ大統領、国連改革求める　サウジ・フーシ派停戦へ仲介継続
items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary: [アンカラ ２２日 ロイター] -
items.body:
[アンカラ ２２日 ロイター] - トルコのエルドアン大統領は２２日、国連総会で演説し、国連は平和維持の責務を果たせなくなっていると指摘した上で、安全保障理事会の改革を求めた。

エルドアン氏は数年前から、安保理をより包括的で幅広い構造にするよう求めてきた。「１９０カ国以上の意思が５カ国の気まぐれに左右される制度は、公平でもなければ、信頼を十分に築くことができるものでもないと認識するべきだ」と述べた。また、「８１年前に設立された国連は、この使命を果たせなくなっている。むしろ、果たせないようにされてしまった」と続けた。

エルドアン氏はパレスチナ自治区ガザの状況も非難し、「良心を持つ者ならば、現地で起きていることに目を背けることはできない」と語った。

パレスチナ自治政府のアッバス議長が２年連続で国連総会の場に姿を見せられていないことについても不当だと批判。パレスチナ国家を承認していない国々に再考を促し、全ての国に対し、ガザでの戦争終結に向けてイスラエルへの圧力を強めるよう呼びかけた。

エルドアン氏はまた、イエメンの親イラン武装組織フーシ派とサウジアラビアの戦闘を終結させるため、トルコが全ての関係者と協力して努力を続けていると述べ、戦闘の継続は誰の利益にもならないと強調した。

その上で、トルコは紛争終結に向けた外交努力を維持していくと表明した。

フーシ派は、イエメンで戦闘が再び激化する中、サウジアラビアへの攻撃を強めている。

items.title: CNN, CBS News oversight board will be 'toothless,' experts warn
items.author: Jaspreet Singh
items.creator: Jaspreet Singh
items.summary: Experts warn that David Ellison's promise of editorial independence for CNN and CBS News after the Paramount merger is a hollow one.
items.body:
David Ellison is set to [USN:L4N45D112 TEXT:"take control"] of two of the biggest news organizations in the US after his Paramount Skydance (PSKY.O) completes its takeover of Warner Bros Discovery (WBD.O) , giving him wide influence over the news media landscape. But experts warn his promise of editorial independence for CNN and CBS News is a hollow one.
Ellison agreed to create an editorial independence board to oversee CNN and CBS as part of Monday's [USN:L4N45D1A9 TEXT:"settlement"] with a coalition of 12 US states and a Hollywood writers' union. The group will be made up of five veteran journalists, to "establish guiding editorial and journalism principles for the combined entity's news channels," according to the agreement.
[USN:L6N45D0SG TEXT:"Skepticism abounds"]. "Genuine oversight of a news organization is provided by its editors and owners. If they are not committed to doing things honorably themselves, nobody they appoint and pay can possibly be expected to do it for them," said Dan Gillmor, a retired journalist and educator.
"Of course" the board will be toothless, he said.
Notably, the board, whose members will be appointed and paid by the combined entity, is not explicitly granted investigative oversight and the binding nature of its decisions is unclear, leaving final authority in the hands of Ellison.
Some of CNN's current and former staff are also questioning the settlement. Prominent journalist Kara Swisher said earlier this year that she plans to leave the network "as soon as I can" due to the Paramount takeover and dismissing the independence board as a "fig leaf."
"Ellison's record at CBS so far is not encouraging and is even troubling. I think he is a very pleasant person, … That hardly matters, as I am only interested in how he behaves as a media owner. So far, I am not impressed," Swisher told Reuters.
California Attorney General Rob Bonta said the board is a meaningful way to protect the integrity of CNN and CBS.
'ENFORCEMENT GAPS' The settlement also creates [USN:L4N45D1A9 TEXT:"an independent monitoring trustee"] with broad authority over film production and cable-licensing, but the trustee shall have "no role or authority relating to the Combined Entity's news operations."
"That's a remarkable carveout," said Jonathan Peters, a media law professor at the University of Georgia.
He said the settlement is not without legal merit because states have the power to enforce it in federal court, but there is a "significant enforcement gap" regarding editorial independence.
The concerns are also fueled by [USN:L1N43G107 TEXT:"lawmakers' criticism of Ellison"] for tailoring news coverage at Paramount-owned CBS News to favor President Donald Trump. Critics fear how he would manage Warner's CNN once it comes under his ownership.
There is also no provision that requires the board's findings and decisions to be made public.
The companies said the board would also resolve internal disputes over reporting bias and disputes between news staff and management at CNN and CBS.
Board members will serve three-year terms and are protected against arbitrary dismissal by a "good cause" removal standard, though the company retains exclusive authority to fill all vacancies.
"It's unclear how the attorneys general or courts can constitutionally hold Paramount accountable for the board's actions or inaction without themselves interfering in content," said Seth Stern, a media lawyer and chief of advocacy at the Freedom of the Press Foundation.
WALL STREET JOURNAL PRECEDENT The new owner will get about a six-month window to reshape newsroom leadership before any oversight begins, as the board will be established only within 180 days of the merger.
The idea of an independent oversight board is not new. When Rupert Murdoch's News Corp (NWSA.O) bought the Wall Street Journal in 2007, it agreed to establish a special committee to protect the objectivity and independence of its publications.
The group is meant to guard against corporate interference and it must approve changes to the Journal's top editors, but it does not assess or comment on editorial coverage.
Even so, it is considered powerless.
"When Murdoch wanted to install his own loyal lieutenant as top editor in 2008, he just did it, the board was left in the dust," Bill Grueskin, a faculty member at Columbia Journalism School and former deputy managing editor of the Wall Street Journal, said in an emailed response.
Grueskin sees little difference in Ellison's concessions to editorial independence.
"The owner calls the shots," he said. "The responsibilities and rights of Ellison's board are exceptionally vague.

items.title: Trump warns in UN speech he could 'annihilate' Iran without peace deal
items.author: CNA
items.summary: US President Donald Trump said the US may make a deal with Iran after the midterm elections, but warned that he could take stronger military action if Iran does not agree.
items.body:
Advertisement

World

Trump warns in UN speech he could 'annihilate' Iran without peace deal

US President Donald Trump said the US may make a deal with Iran after the midterm elections, but warned that he could take stronger military action if Iran does not agree.

US President Donald Trump gestures on the sidelines of the 81st United Nations General Assembly in New York City, US, Sep 22, 2026. (Photo: REUTERS/Toby Melville)

UNITED NATIONS: US President Donald Trump used his UN General Assembly speech on Tuesday (Sep 22) to make the case for his war on Iran, arguing he has prevented Tehran from obtaining a nuclear weapon and warning that he could "annihilate the Islamic Republic" if no deal is reached to end the conflict.
While predicting his administration would strike a peace deal with Iran following t he Nov 3 US midterm elections , Trump called on other nations to join America in isolating Iran economically to force it to the negotiating table.
"I have a big decision to make. Will a deal be made with Iran that lets them rebuild and create a far greater country than it ever was before?" Trump said. "Or do I annihilate the Islamic Republic and do it quickly, never giving them a chance to kill and destroy people and countries again?"
He later told reporters at the United Nations that US officials had had a "very good" three-hour meeting on Tuesday with the Iranian delegation.

Since returning to office last year for a second term, Trump has sent waves through the global order, joining Israel to attack Iran, ordering a raid on Venezuela that captured the country's leader, and threatening to seize Greenland.
In a 37-minute speech ahead of a whirlwind diplomatic schedule that included meetings with the leaders of Britain, Ukraine and Japan, Trump laid out his foreign policy vision, arguing that the Iran war had spared the world the threat of a nuclear-armed menace while asserting US dominance in the Western Hemisphere is essential to preventing crises from taking root.
"Our actions in Venezuela are proof that the United States will no longer permit threats to America to gain a foothold anywhere in the Western Hemisphere," Trump said. "While others have spoken of peace, I have made peace."

Related:

Binance faces US scrutiny over possible Iran sanctions violations, source says

Iran, US hint at revival of talks as Trump, Pezeshkian due to attend UN

Outside the UN headquarters, dozens of anti-Iranian-government demonstrators gathered, a few of them holding up signs calling for democracy and decrying dictatorship.
Trump brushed aside suggestions that the midterm elections, in which his Republican Party risks losing control of Congress, could constrain his handling of the war. Some analysts have argued that a Democratic takeover of the legislature would weaken his leverage in the conflict.
"What they don't realize is that I'm not running," Trump said, referring to the leadership in Tehran. “I did that already, and won in a landslide. We won in a giant landslide, and I'll be here for 2-1/2 years.”
DIPLOMATIC WHIRLWIND Taking aim at US neighbours, Trump labelled Mexico "the epicentre of cartel violence," urged its government to "reclaim control of its soil," and said his administration was pursuing "a fundamental change in the situation in Cuba."
Members of the Cuban delegation walked out of the hall as Trump referenced his pressure campaign against the country.
"It's an absolutely failed state, it's failing like never before, and it will fall," said Trump .
Yet Trump 's appearance was less dramatic than in 2025, when he used a combative speech to chastise world leaders, warning that some countries were "going to hell," and complained about UN facilities after being briefly stranded on a malfunctioning escalator and suffering an initial teleprompter failure.
Trump renewed his criticism of the UN, highlighting his efforts to cut its bureaucracy, but offered no fresh attacks or indications that the US would leave any additional UN agencies.

Related:

Trump returns to UN at a moment of anxiety about Iran, AI and the future of world body itself

Commentary: Trump declares victory in Greenland, but the deal exposes a deeper crisis of trust

Trump spoke less than a week after a UN fact-finding mission said it had reasonable grounds to believe US forces committed war crimes in two strikes on Iran, including one that hit a primary school in the southern city of Minab.
He renewed his criticism of international bodies that could serve as a check on US power, singling out the International Criminal Court and declaring that US military personnel would not be subject to its authority.
"We will never allow US service members or anyone else to be investigated or given show trials by an anti-American tribunal with no jurisdiction over us," he said.
Ahead of a UN Security Council meeting on AI and international security on Wednesday, Trump acknowledged the challenges of the new technology but said, "I'm not going to stifle growth of something that will be bigger than the Industrial Revolution."
The speech kicked off a day of high-level diplomacy at the United Nations, where Trump was due to meet more than a dozen world leaders as wars in the Middle East and Ukraine continued to test his foreign policy agenda.
British Prime Minister Andy Burnham said he had "established a good connection" with Trump in their first-ever meeting, where they discussed trade, Ukraine and the status of the Falkland Islands.
At the press-facing start of their talks, Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi said the meeting would demonstrate the strength of the US-Japan alliance amid a "severe security environment, including in Asia," an apparent nod to China. Trump is due to meet Chinese President Xi Jinping in Washington later this week.
On his meeting with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy, Trump told reporters that the two talked about finding a solution to end Russia's war in Ukraine.

Source: Reuters/fs

items.title: Retornos bonos Tesoro EEUU caen, inversores evalúan expectativas de tasas y baja del petróleo
items.author: Caroline Valetkevitch
items.creator: Caroline Valetkevitch
items.summary: Los rendimientos de los bonos del Tesoro de Estados Unidos bajaron el martes, mientras los inversores sopesaban la caída de los precios del petróleo frente a las expectativas de que la Reserva Federal suba nuevamente las tasas de interés.
items.body:
Los rendimientos de los bonos del Tesoro de Estados Unidos bajaron el martes, mientras los inversores sopesaban la caída de los precios del petróleo frente a las expectativas de que la Reserva Federal suba nuevamente las tasas de interés.
El retorno a dos años, que suele evolucionar en consonancia con las expectativas sobre las tasas de interés de la Fed, alcanzó un nuevo máximo de dos años, en 4,7879%, pero luego perdía 2,5 puntos básicos, a 4,728%.
Los precios del petróleo cerraron a la baja, después de que el presidente de Estados Unidos, Donald Trump, dijo a periodistas en Naciones Unidas que los funcionarios estadounidenses habían mantenido el martes una "muy buena" reunión de tres horas con la delegación iraní.
Trump también dijo durante un discurso ante la Asamblea General de la ONU que creía que Washington alcanzaría un acuerdo con Irán tras las elecciones legislativas que se celebrarán a principios de noviembre.
Los precios del crudo se han disparado desde el inicio de la guerra de Estados Unidos e Israel contra Irán, lo que ha avivado el temor a la inflación y a un aumento de las tasas de interés.
La Fed subió el costo del crédito la semana pasada por primera vez desde 2023 para intentar controlar la inflación. Los operadores estiman que hay aproximadamente un 55% de probabilidad de otro incremento cuando el banco central se reúna en octubre, según CME FedWatch.
El presidente de la Fed de Richmond, Tom Barkin, dijo el martes que las subidas de tasas de la Fed y la amenaza de que haya más podrían moderar las expectativas de inflación de las empresas y frenar los aumentos de precios, a medida que estas negocian los presupuestos para el próximo año.
La presidenta de la Fed de Boston, Susan Collins, escribió el martes en LinkedIn que apoyaba la decisión tomada la semana pasada por el banco central de subir las tasas ante los riesgos de que la inflación futura se sitúe sobre el 2%.
Los rendimientos de referencia de los bonos estadounidenses a 10 años se mantuvieron bajo el 5%, tras alcanzar el 5,041% la semana pasada, el máximo desde 2007.
Los rendimientos a 10 años bajaron 2,2 puntos básicos, a 4,941%, y los de 30 años retrocedieron 1,5 puntos básicos, al 5,281%.
Un indicador muy seguido de la curva de rendimientos, que mide la diferencia entre las tasas a dos y 10 años , y que se considera un indicador de las expectativas económicas, se situaba en 21,1 puntos básicos.
items.raw_description: Los rendimientos de los bonos del Tesoro de Estados Unidos bajaron el martes, mientras los inversores sopesaban la caída de los precios del petróleo frente a las expectativas de que la Reserva Federal suba nuevamente las tasas de interés.

items.title: Trump hails Burnham as 'natural business person' after first meeting
items.author: Elizabeth Piper
items.creator: Elizabeth Piper
items.summary: US President Donald Trump hailed Andy Burnham on Tuesday as a "natural business person" at what the new British leader's team described as a smooth first face-to-face meeting.
items.body:
US President Donald Trump hailed Andy Burnham on Tuesday as a "natural business person" at what the new British leader's team described as a smooth first face-to-face meeting.
After days of preparation for the Trump meeting, Burnham emerged relatively unscathed, with the US leader only taking issue with what he called a "terrible deal" to cede sovereignty of the [USN:L6N45D0ZR TEXT:"Chagos Islands,"] home to a US-British air base.
Otherwise, Trump praised Burnham, saying Britain's seventh prime minister in a decade was someone with whom he could do business and a patriot who had put Britain on the up after replacing the former prime minister, Keir Starmer, in July.
"I think right now, based on my relationship with the prime minister, Andy, I think that ... we're doing very well," Trump said after they met on the sidelines of the United Nations General Assembly in New York for around 40 minutes.
"I think he's a natural business person. We've had a lot of discussions, even before this meeting we were talking with each other numerous times on the phone."
'ENCOURAGING MEETING' Burnham, who travelled to New York on Monday to take part in the UN assembly, had said little beforehand about his expectations for the meeting with Trump, saying only that in their two phone calls he had found "a connection" with the US president.
Afterwards, he repeated that earlier conversations had established that connection "and that very much came through today".
"(I) can certainly work with him. It was a very encouraging meeting," Burnham told reporters, saying the two leaders had found "common ground" on dealing with cost-of-living pressures, ending the conflict in the Middle East and reindustrialising nations to spur economic growth, among other issues.
"He was very upbeat about the country's (Britain's) prospects, which, to be honest, was great to hear."
Before arriving in New York, Burnham had sought common ground with Trump on AI, a focus of his comments to the UN on Monday in which he described the technology as having the ability to bring "huge benefits" to the British and global economy.
Trump has said he wants to cherish AI rather than stifle its growth, dismissing fears about it as a hoax and "sick conspiracy". The US leader has said concerns can be addressed through the existing [USN:L6N45E0RD TEXT:"justice system"] without extra regulation — an issue that might cause some friction with Britain.
Yet, while the two leaders seemed to find common ground on a number of issues, there were some pitfalls.
Trump again criticised Britain's move, under Starmer, to cede sovereignty of the Chagos Islands while retaining control of Diego Garcia air base on a 99-year lease.
Trump called the agreement with Mauritius, now on hold, a "terrible" deal. "It's amazing how strategic it is, and I think the prime minister is going to be looking at it," he said.
Burnham later told reporters he had inherited the problem and would work to find a resolution between the different sides. "It was clear that we need to come to that agreement, but I'm confident we can find it working with our US partners," he said.
Burnham also showed a willingness to disagree with Trump if it is in his nation's interest, saying he would "stand firm in the face of any threats" to the right of Falkland Islanders to self-determination and to remain British.
In August, Trump said he was reviewing the United States' neutral position on the remote archipelago in the South Atlantic. Days later Argentine President Javier Milei — who will address the UN on Wednesday — said he would impose sanctions on oil companies drilling in the islands.
And the British leader navigated some other bilateral sticking points. Trump appeared unmoved over Britain's decision to block imports from [USN:L8N45007X TEXT:"Israeli settlements"] in the occupied West Bank, while its decision not to back the US over the Iran war was also skated over.
OPENS WAY FOR BURNHAM TO FOCUS ON AI With the meeting done, Burnham turns his focus for UNGA to AI and his support for the technology, which he hopes will help Britain assume a leading role globally.
At an earlier business roundtable, Burnham said he would make the case for Britain in a speech later on Tuesday to help establish "a single set of global principles and standards" to unlock the potential of AI.
Describing Britain as being stuck in 10 years of political turbulence since voting to leave the European Union in 2016, Burnham told business leaders he wanted to usher in a period of stability and embrace AI, while being clear-eyed on the risks.
"So outside Downing Street, on my first day, I said I want to be the circuit breaker," he told the roundtable, including Tim Cook, executive chairman of Apple, and Citigroup CEO Jane Fraser.
"(To) bring forward a very clear path that everyone can understand, a 10-year plan for Britain ... so that nobody's in any doubt at all about what we're trying to do."
